course.description: A practical evaluation checklist for finance leaders choosing an AI-native FP&A or forecasting tool — plus stage-based recommendations from startup to scale. Adapted from Alyona Mysko's LinkedIn post.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in 5 Questions to Ask Any Forecasting Tool Before You Sign.

activities.title: Does It Connect Directly to Your Accounting System?

lessons.content:
**Question 1: Does it connect directly to my accounting system? Or does it just import CSVs?**

This is your first filter. If the tool only accepts CSV uploads, you're signing up for manual refresh forever. Every time you want an updated forecast, someone on your team has to:

1. Export data from your accounting system
2. Format it to match the tool's import template
3. Upload it manually
4. Hope nothing broke in the translation

A direct integration means the tool pulls live data from your GL, your ERP, your bank feeds. The forecast stays current without human intervention.

**Red flag:** If the vendor says "we support CSV import" as their primary data connection method, that's not AI-native — that's a spreadsheet with extra steps.
lessons.title: Does It Connect Directly to Your Accounting System?

activities.title: Does It Support Rolling Forecasts by Default?

lessons.content:
**Question 2: Does it support rolling forecasts by default? Or are you locked into quarterly snapshots?**

Static quarterly forecasts are a relic of the pre-AI era. By the time you finish building the Q3 forecast, half the assumptions are already stale.

Rolling forecasts continuously extend the planning horizon — typically 12-18 months forward — and update as new actuals come in. This gives you:

- Always-current visibility into the next 12+ months
- Faster response to changing business conditions
- No more "forecast season" crunch

**What to look for:** The tool should make rolling forecasts the default behavior, not a premium add-on or custom configuration. If you have to request it, the tool was built for a different era.
lessons.title: Does It Support Rolling Forecasts by Default?

activities.title: Can You Build Scenarios Without a Consultant?

lessons.content:
**Question 3: Can I build my own scenarios without a consultant?**

If you need to file a support ticket to model a 30% marketing cut, **run.**

Scenario modeling should be self-service. You should be able to:

- Create a new scenario in minutes, not days
- Adjust any assumption (headcount, revenue growth, spend categories) yourself
- Compare scenarios side-by-side instantly
- Share scenarios with stakeholders without exporting to PowerPoint

**The test:** Ask the vendor: "If my CEO calls at 4pm and wants to see what happens if we cut marketing spend by 30% and delay hiring by one quarter, how long does it take me to build that scenario?" If the answer involves their services team, it's not the right tool.
lessons.title: Can You Build Scenarios Without a Consultant?

lessons.content:
**Question 4: Does it have real AI? Can it draft commentary, flag anomalies, build new views?**

Many tools slap a chat box on top of dashboards and call it "AI-powered." That's not AI — that's a search bar.

Real AI in a forecasting tool should:

- **Draft variance commentary** — explain why actuals deviated from plan in natural language
- **Flag anomalies** — surface unusual patterns you might miss (a cost center spiking, revenue trending below plan)
- **Build new views** — create ad-hoc analyses from natural language requests
- **Learn from your corrections** — get better at predictions and commentary over time

**The test:** Ask for a live demo where the AI explains a variance in your data. If it can only show pre-built dashboards with a chat overlay, it's not what you need.
lessons.title: Does It Have Real AI?

lessons.content:
**Question 5: How fast is setup? If the answer is 3 months — it's not AI-native. Full stop.**

This is the tell. Legacy FP&A tools repackaged with AI features still carry legacy implementation timelines. A truly AI-native tool should be:

- **Connected to your data** in days, not months
- **Producing usable forecasts** within the first week
- **Fully operational** without a dedicated implementation consultant

**The right tool depends on your stage:**

| Stage | Recommendation |
|-------|---------------|
| **$0–5M ARR** | Claude + Google Sheets. Low setup. Good through Series A. |
| **$5–20M ARR** | Claude + MCP (Fuel or any AI-native FP&A tool). Manual exports break at this scale. |
| **$20M+ ARR** | Claude + MCP (Fuel or any AI-native FP&A tool). Full connected stack. Live dashboards. Multi-entity support. |

The key insight: at every stage, Claude can serve as your AI reasoning layer while your FP&A tool handles the data infrastructure. The combination is more powerful than either alone.
lessons.title: How Fast Is Setup?
